editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Algebra 10.103, Definitions 10.103.1, 10.103.8, and 10.103.12. It distinguishes Cohen–Macaulay modules at a Noetherian local ring, maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules, and their localization-based extension to arbitrary Noetherian rings.

definitions.text: A finitely generated module M over a Noetherian local ring R is Cohen–Macaulay if depth_R(M) equals the Krull dimension of the support Supp_R(M).
A finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay if depth_R(M)=dim(R), not merely the dimension of its possibly smaller support.
A finite module M over a Noetherian ring R is Cohen–Macaulay if for each prime p the localized module M_p is Cohen–Macaulay over the local ring R_p.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Schemes 26.6, Lemmas 26.6.1 and 26.6.4. The section identifies the contravariant relationship between commutative rings and affine schemes through maps of their spectra.

definitions.text: For commutative rings A and B, a morphism Spec(B)→Spec(A) of affine schemes is equivalently determined by a ring homomorphism A→B, acting on prime ideals by inverse image.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: affine scheme morphisms and ring maps

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Categories 4.29, Definition 4.29.1 and Definition 4.29.4. A strict 2-category has categories of 1- and 2-morphisms with strictly associative horizontal composition, whereas equivalence of objects needs inverse 1-morphisms only up to invertible 2-morphisms.

definitions.text: A strict 2-category consists of objects, hom-categories whose objects are 1-morphisms and arrows are 2-morphisms, and strictly associative and unital composition functors between hom-categories satisfying the interchange law.
Two objects X,Y in a 2-category are equivalent if there are 1-morphisms F:X→Y and G:Y→X with invertible 2-morphisms FG⇒id_Y and GF⇒id_X.
definitions.context_hint: Higher category theory: equivalence of 2-category objects

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Commutative Algebra 10.26, Lemma 10.26.1. The irreducible components of Spec(R) are precisely the closed subsets V(p) for minimal prime ideals p.

definitions.text: For a commutative ring R, the irreducible components of Spec(R) are exactly the subsets V(p) where p ranges over prime ideals minimal under inclusion.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: irreducible components of the prime spectrum

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Topology 5.15, Definition 5.15.1. Constructibility uses finite Boolean combinations of retrocompact opens and is distinguished from being constructible only on some open cover.

definitions.text: A subset E of a topological space X is constructible if it is a finite union of sets U\V with U and V open and retrocompact in X.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: constructible subset using retrocompact opens

definitions.text: A subset E of X is locally constructible if there exists an open cover (V_i) of X such that E∩V_i is constructible as a subset of V_i for each i.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Categories 4.13, Definition 4.13.1. The monomorphism condition is left cancellation, whereas epimorphism is right cancellation; these cannot generally be identified with injection or surjection outside Set.

definitions.text: A morphism f:X→Y in a category C is a monomorphism if for every object W and maps a,b:W→X, the equality f∘a=f∘b implies a=b.
A morphism f:X→Y in a category C is an epimorphism if for every object W and maps a,b:Y→W, equality a∘f=b∘f implies a=b.
